# Psalm 59 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. According to Do Not Destroy. A Miktam of David, when Saul sent men to watch his house in order to kill him.

**2** Deliver me from my enemies, O my God; protect me from those who rise up against me;

**3** deliver me from those who work evil, and save me from bloodthirsty men.

**4** For behold, they lie in wait for my life; fierce men stir up strife against me. For no transgression or sin of mine, O LORD,

**5** for no fault of mine, they run and make ready. Awake, come to meet me, and see!

**6** You, LORD God of hosts, are God of Israel. Rouse Yourself to punish all the nations; spare none of those who treacherously plot evil. Selah.

**7** Each evening they come back, howling like dogs and prowling about the city.

**8** There they are, bellowing with their mouths with swords in their lips — for 'Who,' they think, 'will hear us?'

**9** But You, O LORD, laugh at them; You hold all the nations in derision.

**10** O my Strength, I will watch for You, for You, O God, are my fortress.

**11** My God in His steadfast love will meet me; God will let me look in triumph on my enemies.

**12** Kill them not, lest my people forget; make them totter by Your power and bring them down, O Lord, our shield!

**13** For the sin of their mouths, the words of their lips, let them be trapped in their pride. For the cursing and lies that they utter,

**14** consume them in wrath; consume them till they are no more, that they may know that God rules over Jacob to the ends of the earth. Selah.

**15** Each evening they come back, howling like dogs and prowling about the city.

**16** They wander about for food and growl if they do not get their fill.

**17** But I will sing of Your strength; I will sing aloud of Your steadfast love in the morning. For You have been to me a fortress and a refuge in the day of my distress.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **59:1**: 1 Samuel 19:11 — Michal helps David escape through a window while Saul's men surround the house. The psalm is a prayer during a siege.

— LOGOS
